endorsements.quote: If provided a relevant patient-facing API, patients can grant, revoke, renew or update their consent across the network directly, reducing the need for manual data entry by a local project manager and minimizing the possibility of manipulation, such as inclusion of fake or ineligible (non-consented; expired/revoked) data in attempt to bias models.

Any implementation of smart contracts should thus be done not only with patient preferences but also, ideally, with community deliberation and input, 55 fostering community engagement in clinical research.

unlisted_practices: Integrate smart contracts into federated and swarm learning frameworks to automate, enforce, and immutably document patient-level consent for data use.
Design smart contract terms to align incentives across multiple stakeholders, including physicians, hospitals, research institutions, community-based organizations, and industry partners.
Involve legal scholars, ethicists, and social scientists in designing smart contracts so they serve patient, community, and societal interests.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual framework and commentary article proposing the integration of smart contracts with federated learning to automate and govern patient consent, rather than an empirical trial or benchmark.
